nodes.description: Recorded as a negative phenotype because it separates FHH2, like FHH1, from primary hyperparathyroidism. It deliberately carries no phenotype_term and no frequency: binding HP:0000787 here would export as the opposite assertion. The evidence is a single kindred, so the claim is that renal calcification is not a feature of the reported cases, not that it never occurs.

nodes.description: Cinacalcet sensitises the calcium-sensing receptor on the parathyroid chief cell, acting at the receptor upstream of the GNA11 signalling defect, so that more signal passes through the partly functional mutant G-alpha-11 and parathyroid hormone secretion falls. The relation to the nodes above is pharmacological compensation, not causation, so this node asserts no downstream edge.

nodes.description: Patchy hypomineralisation of primary and permanent enamel, reported in two families carrying a whole-gene GNA11 deletion or an early frameshift. Gna11 and G-alpha-11 are expressed in mouse ameloblasts and odontoblasts, and heterozygous Gna11 mice have delayed and reduced enamel mineralisation, which suggests a direct role for G-alpha-11 in tooth formation. Whether the missense alleles behind most FHH2 kindreds produce the same defect is unknown.

Global Gna11 knockout mice have hypercalcaemia and mildly raised PTH, and also raised serum FGF23 with hypophosphataemia and, in homozygotes, systemic inflammation. Whether FGF23 is raised in human FHH2 has not been reported, so the FGF23 finding is recorded here only as a model observation.

A germline missense, in-frame deletion or frameshift variant in GNA11 that reduces the ability of G-alpha-11 to transmit CaSR activation to phospholipase C. Reported alleles include Leu135Gln, Ile200del, Thr54Met, Phe220Ser, Thr347Ala, the frameshifts His327LeufsTer150 and Ser18ArgfsTer2, and a whole-gene deletion. Structural work places the defects at the interface between the helical and GTPase domains (Thr54Met) and in the hydrophobic cleft that binds phospholipase C (Phe220Ser).

nodes.description: In the kidney the CaSR-G-alpha-11 pathway normally reduces tubular calcium reabsorption when blood calcium rises. With G-alpha-11 weakened, calcium is retained, so urinary calcium is low or inappropriately normal for the prevailing serum calcium. The renal mechanism is inferred from the CaSR pathway and from mouse data rather than measured directly in FHH2 patients.
